result.question:
Survey recent (2024–2026) publications and methods in generative models for drug/molecule design, scoped to what is most actionable for a project building an all-atom, pocket-conditioned CYCLIC-PEPTIDE generator (current baseline: PepGLAD, geometric latent diffusion). Cover and compare, with citations:

1. State-of-the-art all-atom / full-atom molecular generation (diffusion, flow-matching, and successors) — e.g. successors to TargetDiff/DiffSBDD, all-atom flow-matching models, and what now leads structure-based drug design benchmarks.
2. Peptide and CYCLIC-peptide de novo design — PepGLAD, PepFlow, RFpeptides/RFdiffusion for macrocycles, PepTune, and any 2025–2026 methods; especially macrocyclization/closure handling, non-natural monomers (N-methylation, D-amino acids, stapled), and how they represent/enforce cyclic topology.
3. Unified / multi-modal generators across modalities (small molecule + peptide + protein/antibody + PROTAC/glue) — e.g. UniMoMo, BoltzGen, Boltz-2-based generation — the "one backbone, per-modality plugin" direction.
4. Property- and developability-guided / conditioned generation — permeability, stability, multi-objective; differentiable guidance vs classifier-guidance vs conditioning vs RL/active-learning; how they steer chemistry (not just geometry) properties.
5. Evaluation practice — designability/self-consistency (fold-back scRMSD), DockQ, ΔG, and why AAR is (or isn't) used; standard automated metrics for de novo design.

For each, note the method's key idea, what it improves over prior work, reported numbers where available, and code availability. Conclude with the 3–5 methods/ideas most worth adopting to improve a cyclic-peptide all-atom generator beyond PepGLAD, and any that specifically address the permeability/N-methylation and macrocyclic-closure gaps.
result.summary: For a pocket-conditioned, all-atom cyclic-peptide generator whose baseline is PepGLAD (geometric latent diffusion), the 2024–2026 literature points to four actionable directions. (1) Cyclic-topology handling is now a solved-in-principle problem via two distinct mechanisms worth adopting: RFpeptides' cyclic relative positional encoding (N-/C-termini treated as covalently linked by flipping positive to negative relative positions past the halfway point), and BoltzGen/PepTune's explicit covalent-bond specification, which additionally covers disulfide/head-to-tail/stapled ("helicon") cyclization and non-natural monomers by operating over covalent-bond graphs or peptide SMILES. (2) The strongest architectural trend is unification: UniMoMo (the direct PepGLAD lineage extension) and BoltzGen show that a single all-atom model jointly trained across peptides/antibodies/small molecules beats domain-specific models, with BoltzGen adding geometry-based residue encoding (14 atoms per residue) and extensive wet-lab validation. (3) For chemistry/developability steering (the permeability + N-methylation gap), PepTune is the most on-point: discrete diffusion over peptide SMILES with Monte Carlo Tree Guidance (MCTG) to simultaneously optimize permeability, solubility, hemolysis, non-fouling, and binding affinity at inference time without retraining. (4) Small-molecule SBDD lessons transfer as engineering practices: flow-matching (FLOWR / FLOWR.root) beats diffusion on validity/pose/speed and can unify generation+affinity scoring, and controlled ablations show explicit-hydrogen training, large-scale unconditional pretraining, and high-quality crystallographic data each materially improve 3D generation quality. The 3–5 highest-value adoptions: cyclic positional encoding or explicit covalent-bond conditioning for closure; a SMILES/covalent-bond representation to admit N-methylation/D-amino-acids/staples; MCTG-style inference-time multi-objective guidance for permeability; and flow-matching plus pretraining/hydrogen/data-quality engineering carried over from SBDD.

findings.claim: Cyclic topology can be enforced two complementary ways worth adopting over PepGLAD: (a) RFpeptides' cyclic relative positional encoding, which treats N- and C-termini as covalently linked by switching positive to negative relative position encodings once an index is more than halfway around the peptide; and (b) explicit covalent-bond specification (BoltzGen, PepTune), which additionally covers disulfide-stapled, head-to-tail, and arbitrary cyclization plus stapled 'helicon' peptides.
findings.evidence: RFpeptides (Nature Chem Biol 2025, PMC11601608) cyclizes RFdiffusion/RoseTTAFold2 positional encodings by 'switching from positive relative position encodings to negative encodings when index j is more than halfway around the peptide relative to index i,' enabling macrocyclic backbones with N-/C-termini covalently linked. BoltzGen (bioRxiv 2025.11.20.689494) supports cyclic peptides 'by specifying a covalent bond,' including 'disulfide-stapled peptides, head-to-tail cyclic peptides, and any other type of cyclization,' plus helicons via a staple molecule bonded to two cysteine sulfurs (disulfide-cyclized sizes 10-18 validated against RagA:RagC, ~88% experimental confirmation). PepTune enforces valid cyclic SMILES via a bond-dependent masking schedule and invalid-loss function.

findings.claim: PepTune is the most directly relevant method for closing the chemistry/developability gap (permeability, N-methylation, non-natural monomers): it runs discrete diffusion directly over peptide SMILES (Masked Discrete Language Model + bond-dependent masking + invalid-loss for valid cyclic/modified structures) and steers generation with Monte Carlo Tree Guidance (MCTG), an inference-time multi-objective guidance algorithm that simultaneously optimizes membrane permeability, solubility, hemolysis, non-fouling, and binding affinity without retraining.
findings.evidence: PepTune (PMLR v267 tang25n, ICML 2025; arXiv:2412.17780) is 'a multi-objective discrete diffusion model for simultaneous generation and optimization of therapeutic peptide SMILES,' trained on ~11M peptide SMILES 'including a wide array of non-natural amino acids and various cyclization patterns.' Built on MDLM with 'a novel bond-dependent masking schedule and invalid loss function.' MCTG is 'an inference-time multi-objective guidance algorithm that balances exploration and exploitation to iteratively refine Pareto-optimal sequences' integrating 'classifier-based rewards' with 'no additional training.' Simultaneously optimizes 'target binding affinity, membrane permeability, solubility, hemolysis, and non-fouling.'

findings.claim: The strongest architectural direction is a single unified all-atom model jointly trained across modalities, which outperforms domain-specific generators. UniMoMo is the direct PepGLAD lineage extension (same geometric latent diffusion + iterative full-atom autoencoder + E(3)-equivariant diffusion, extended to peptides/antibodies/small molecules via a shared 'graph of blocks' representation), and multi-domain joint training empirically beats single-modality training on the same architecture.
findings.evidence: UniMoMo (arXiv:2503.19300, ICML 2025, same first author as PepGLAD) is 'the first framework capable of designing binders of multiple molecular domains using a single model,' unifying molecules 'as graphs of blocks, where each block corresponds to either a standard amino acid or a molecular fragment,' via 'a geometric latent diffusion model...featuring an iterative full-atom autoencoder to compress blocks into latent space points, followed by an E(3)-equivariant diffusion process.' Controlled UniMoMo(single) vs UniMoMo(all) ablation shows joint training wins across metrics: peptides AAR 37.59->39.45%, C-RMSD 2.48->2.19, deltaG -28.72->-34.35, IMP 29.03->40.86%; antibodies AAR 48.78->52.34%. Caveat: gains may reflect larger total data, not only cross-domain transfer; peptide diversity slightly reduced (JSDbb 0.390->0.205).

findings.claim: BoltzGen demonstrates that a single all-atom diffusion model can unify binder design and structure prediction across all target modalities (proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, peptides, enzymes, disordered regions) using a purely geometry-based residue encoding (14 atoms per residue whose placement determines identity), with strong experimental validation - a compelling template for a unified cyclic-peptide generator.
findings.evidence: BoltzGen (bioRxiv 2025.11.20.689494; boltz.bio) is 'a single all-atom diffusion model capable of performing both structure prediction and protein design,' where 'each designed residue is represented using 14 atoms' and 'the model determines the residue identity by learning to superpose a subset of the remaining virtual atoms onto designated backbone atoms' (purely geometry-based, avoiding mixed discrete/continuous). It 'unifies design and structure prediction, resulting in a single model that also reaches state-of-the-art folding performance.' Validated across 'eight diverse wetlab design campaigns...across 26 targets,' with 'nanomolar binders for 66% of targets.' MIT-licensed open source.

findings.claim: Flow-matching now leads structure-based (small-molecule) generation and can unify generation with affinity scoring, offering transferable architecture choices for the peptide generator's structure-based conditioning. FLOWR (continuous+categorical flow matching with equivariant optimal transport, pocket-conditioned) beats prior diffusion/flow SBDD methods on PoseBusters-validity, pose accuracy, and interaction recovery while being up to 70x faster; FLOWR.root extends this to a single SE(3)-equivariant backbone doing de novo generation, interaction/pharmacophore-conditional sampling, fragment elaboration, and multi-endpoint affinity prediction (pIC50/pKi/pKd/pEC50).
findings.evidence: FLOWR (arXiv:2504.10564, Nature Comp Sci 2026) 'integrates continuous and categorical flow matching with equivariant optimal transport, enhanced by an efficient protein pocket conditioning,' and 'surpasses current state-of-the-art diffusion- and flow-based methods in terms of PoseBusters-validity, pose accuracy, and interaction recovery' (validity 0.92 vs 0.83 for PILOT) with 'up to 70-fold faster performance.' FLOWR.root (arXiv:2510.02578) is 'an SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching model for pocket-aware 3D ligand generation with joint potency and binding affinity prediction and confidence estimation,' supporting 'de novo generation, interaction- and pharmacophore-conditional sampling, fragment elaboration and replacement.' Caveat: both are small-molecule ligand models; relevance is architectural, not direct peptide methods; FLOWR benchmarks are self-reported on the authors' SPINDR dataset.

findings.claim: Three engineering levers from controlled SBDD ablations reliably improve pocket-conditioned 3D generation quality and are cheap to transfer: (a) explicit-hydrogen generation during training, (b) large-scale unconditional pretraining before pocket-conditioned fine-tuning, and (c) inclusion of high-quality (internal crystallographic) structural data.
findings.evidence: Wang et al. (J. Cheminformatics 2026, PMC13292534), ablating pocket-conditioned SemlaFlow: explicit Hs raise molecular validity 66.11% vs 58.34% and roughly double PoseBusters pass rate 22.3% vs 10.2% (strain energy 15.96->10.59 kcal/mol/atom). GEOM-Drugs pretraining then PDBBind fine-tuning lowers strain energy to 6.58 vs 10.59 kcal/mol/atom from-scratch. Combining internal crystallographic + public data gives the strongest model: 86.20% validity and 46.0% PoseBusters pass vs 69.55% / 27.8% public-only, despite the combined set being smaller. Caveat: all on a SMALL-MOLECULE generator; PoseBusters measures small-molecule chemical validity, not macrocyclic closure, so transfer to peptides is plausible but untested here. Pretraining helped 3D conformation only ('little difference in 2D graph quality').

findings.claim: Boltz-2 provides a jointly-predicting structure+affinity foundation model that can serve as a developability/binding oracle for guidance or scoring in a cyclic-peptide pipeline, filling the affinity gap that AlphaFold3 and Boltz-1 left open.
findings.evidence: Boltz-2 (bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707, MIT Jameel Clinic + Recursion) notes 'AlphaFold3 and Boltz-1...still fall short in predicting binding affinity' and presents 'a new structural biology foundation model that exhibits strong performance for both structure and affinity prediction.' Caveat: the affinity module is scoped to small-molecule-protein binding; and the specific claim that Boltz-2 approaches FEP accuracy at ~1000x speed was REFUTED (0-3) in verification, so treat FEP-parity marketing with skepticism while the joint structure+affinity capability stands.
findings.vote: 3-0 for joint-prediction framing (claim 20); associated FEP-parity/1000x claim was refuted 0-3

result.caveats: Time-sensitivity: several key sources are 2025-2026 preprints not yet peer-reviewed at the depth of the older work - BoltzGen (bioRxiv Nov 2025), FLOWR.root (arXiv Oct 2025), and Boltz-2 (bioRxiv Jun 2025); FLOWR and the SBDD-ablation paper have since been peer-reviewed (Nature Comp Sci 2026, J. Cheminformatics 2026). Benchmark comparisons are frequently self-reported by the authoring team on their own curated datasets (FLOWR on SPINDR, UniMoMo's cross-domain superiority, BoltzGen campaigns), so head-to-head external replication is limited. Modality transfer is the biggest unverified assumption: FLOWR, FLOWR.root, Boltz-2's affinity module, and the PMC13292534 ablations are all small-molecule SBDD results - their lessons (flow-matching, explicit hydrogens, pretraining, crystal-data quality, PoseBusters validity) are plausibly but not empirically shown to transfer to macrocyclic peptides, where closure geometry and non-natural monomers differ fundamentally. Terminology loosening: RFpeptides diffuses backbones (sequence assigned afterward by ProteinMPNN), so it is not strictly 'all-atom' generation; FLOWR's default is heavy-atom (explicit H optional and degrades RDKit validity to 0.64). One refuted claim: Boltz-2 approaching FEP accuracy at ~1000x speed did NOT survive verification (0-3), so avoid citing FEP-parity as established. UniMoMo's multi-domain gains are not disentangled from simply-more-data, and joint training slightly reduced peptide structural diversity.
openQuestions: Do the small-molecule SBDD engineering lessons (explicit-hydrogen training, unconditional pretraining, crystallographic data quality, flow-matching over diffusion) actually transfer to all-atom cyclic-peptide generation, where macrocyclic closure and non-natural monomers dominate, or do peptide-specific inductive biases dominate?

Which cyclization mechanism is superior for a latent-diffusion peptide generator like PepGLAD - RFpeptides-style cyclic relative positional encoding (geometry-native, backbone-level) vs BoltzGen/PepTune-style explicit covalent-bond/SMILES specification (flexible for staples/disulfides/N-methylation but requires representation change) - and can they be combined?

How should permeability and N-methylation guidance be operationalized: PepTune's inference-time MCTG classifier guidance vs differentiable property guidance vs classifier-free conditioning vs RL/active-learning - and what predictor exists for macrocyclic peptide permeability that is accurate enough to steer generation?

What is the standard automated evaluation battery for de novo cyclic-peptide design (designability/self-consistency fold-back scRMSD, DockQ, delta-G, and whether AAR is meaningful for non-natural-monomer peptides), and which of the surveyed methods report on a shared benchmark enabling fair comparison against PepGLAD?

refuted.claim: Boltz-2 is the first deep learning model to approach the accuracy of physics-based free-energy perturbation (FEP) methods while running roughly 1000x faster, making accurate affinity prediction cheap enough for high-throughput screening/optimization loops.
